newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Choppy Australian stocks wander to just firmer end.
newsitem.headline: Choppy Australian stocks wander to just firmer end.

text.p: A choppy Australian share market wandered to a just firmer close on Thursday with futures trading dictating many of the day's gyrations.
The All Ordinaries Index edged 3.8 points higher to 2,627.4.
"The future players have had a big say in many of the moves today," said one Sydney broker, noting that most individual performances matched the broader market's little changed close.
Others echoed similar sentiments, adding that caution appeared to have set in amidst the plethora of key U.S. economic data out this week.

"Retail sales and PPI (producer price index) were out last night but the CPI (consumer price index) figure is out tonight and there is a fairly large emphasis being placed on that in the short term," said Henderson Charlton Jones dealer Hamish Dee.
"I think that's what has driven our market this afternoon -- a little bit of cautiousness heading into tonight."

The big banks got a boost from a buoyant bond market, which strengthened after a surprisingly benign set of final second quarter wages data. However, trader wariness ahead of possible U.S. moves trimmed gains with all four big banks finishing firmer but well off their highs for the day.

Financial services and construction conglomerate Lend Lease Corporation ended 21 cents higher at A$28.97 (US$21.44) after reporting a 15 percent higher year net profit of A$322 million and a lift in final dividend to 50 cents a share.

Construction and contract mining group Leighton Holdings impressed many on the day with a special dividend of 10 cents a share, in addition to a final payout of 13 cents a share, made from a 32 percent higher year net profit of A$86.24 million.
Leighton, which is about 45 percent owned by Germany's Hochtief AG, saw its shares leap six percent to end at A$6.12.

Elsewhere, shares in ferry operator Holyman Ltd plunged 65 cents to end at a record low at A$1.70 as investors jumped ship after Wednesday's profit downgrade due to problems at its 67 percent owned Holyman Sally operations in Europe.
Rises shaded falls by just a whisker, while about 27 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
